pictures.t: Seismotectonic sketch of the Siculo-Calabro Rift Zone
pictures.c: Seismotectonic map of the Siculo-Calabrian Rift Zone, showing a hypothesis of association of the main historical earthquakes with major faults (from Catalano et al. [2008]).
Geological map of the Taormina headland showing location of uplifted marine notches (from Stewart et al. [1997]).

pictures.t: Map of marine terraces of the Taormina headland by Monaco et al. [2002]
pictures.c: Map showing location of Quaternary marine terraces outcropping in the Taormina area (from Monaco et al. [2002]).

pictures.t: Photos and profiles of marine notches
pictures.c: Photos of marine notches and elevation profiles along with location of dated samples (from De Guidi et al. [2003]).
Interpretation of uplifted notches by coseismic and post-seismic displacements (from De Guidi et al. [2003]).

pictures.t: Vertical displacement along the Taormina Fault
pictures.c: Vertical displacement along the Taormina Fault from elevation of marine benchmarcks (from Catalano and De Guidi [2003]).

pictures.t: Sketch of the seismic gap area by Neri et al. [2006]
pictures.c: In this map the Taormina area is interpreted as a seismic gap for large earthquakes (from Neri et al. [2006]).

pictures.t: Location map of seismic profiles across the southern Messina Straits [Argnani et al., 2009]
pictures.c: Position map of seismic profiles used to explore the off-shore of the Taormina Fault. Note the position of the Tao-09 profile (from Argnani et al. [2009]).
Seismic profile TAO-09 running across the expected position of the Taormina Fault and showing undisrupted Plio-Quaternary strata (from Argnani et al. [2009]).
